name: RPF Constable
conductingBody: Railway Recruitment Boards on behalf of the Railway Protection Force (Ministry of Railways)
approxCandidates: ≈45 lakh+ applicants in the CEN RPF 02/2024 cycle (approx.)
eligibility: 10th (Matriculation) pass; 18–28 yrs (relaxation as per rules); physical standards apply

notification.summary: No new RPF Constable notification had been released as of 10 Oct 2026. The last cycle, CEN RPF 02/2024 (≈4,208 Constable posts), held its CBT in March 2025; its CBT result was declared and the PET/PMT, DV and medical stages ran in 2026 as reported. Reports in 2026 expect the next Constable/SI notification, but no official date or vacancy count has been announced.

pattern.notes: No sectional timing; 1/3 negative marking; marks normalised across shifts. Qualifying: UR/OBC/EWS 35%, SC/ST 30%. CBT shortlists candidates for PET (1600 m run for men / 800 m for women, long jump, high jump) and PMT, followed by DV and medical. Questions are of Class 10 standard.

trendAnalysis.summary: Only two recent Constable CBTs exist (CEN 01/2018, held Dec 2018–Feb 2019, and CEN RPF 02/2024, held Mar 2025), so the analysis is based on both. The paper is easy-to-moderate. General Awareness (50 Q) is the largest section: around a fifth is current affairs (sports, awards, schemes), with the rest static GK – history, polity, geography, general science and culture. Arithmetic is direct (number system, percentage, average, profit-loss, SI/CI, time-speed-distance, mensuration). Reasoning is scoring with analogies, series, coding, blood relations, ranking and simple puzzles; non-verbal items (mirror image, embedded figures) appear in small numbers. Good attempts are around 95–105 of 120.

resources.notes: For CEN RPF 02/2024 the question papers, provisional answer keys and response sheets were made available by the RRBs only during the objection window via regional RRB websites (linked from https://www.rrbapply.gov.in). RPF notices are also posted at https://rpf.indianrailways.gov.in. No permanent official PYQ archive; memory-based papers from coaching publishers are unofficial.

questions.question: D. Gukesh, who won the World Chess Championship in December 2024, belongs to which state?
questions.explanation: Gukesh Dommaraju is from Chennai, Tamil Nadu. He defeated Ding Liren in Singapore to win the title.

questions.question: India hosted the G20 Leaders' Summit in September 2023 in which city?
questions.explanation: The 18th G20 Leaders' Summit was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 9–10 September 2023.

questions.question: Which team won the ICC Men's Champions Trophy 2025?
questions.explanation: India beat New Zealand by four wickets in the final at Dubai on 9 March 2025.

questions.question: How many medals in total did India win at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: India won 6 medals – 1 silver (Neeraj Chopra) and 5 bronze (Manu Bhaker; Manu Bhaker & Sarabjot Singh; Swapnil Kusale; men's hockey team; Aman Sehrawat).

questions.question: Which state became the first in independent India to enact and implement its own Uniform Civil Code, in January 2025?
questions.explanation: Uttarakhand implemented its Uniform Civil Code on 27 January 2025, the first state to enact such a law after Independence.

questions.question: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in 1885 at:
questions.explanation: The first session was held in Bombay (Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College) in December 1885 under W. C. Bonnerjee. It was originally planned for Poona but shifted due to a cholera outbreak.

questions.question: Who is popularly known as the 'Iron Man of India'?
questions.explanation: Sardar Patel, India's first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister, integrated the princely states and is called the Iron Man of India.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement after the Chauri Chaura incident, which took place in:
questions.explanation: The Chauri Chaura incident (Gorakhpur district) took place on 4 February 1922; Gandhiji called off the movement soon after.

questions.question: Who is the constitutional head of a State in India?
options: Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.explanation: The Governor is the constitutional (nominal) head of a State; real executive power lies with the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister.

questions.question: The Right to Constitutional Remedies is guaranteed under which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 32 lets citizens move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights; Dr Ambedkar called it the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

questions.question: How many members can the President nominate to the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: Under Article 80, the President nominates 12 members with special knowledge of literature, science, art and social service.

questions.question: Which is the largest ocean in the world?
questions.explanation: The Pacific is the largest and deepest ocean, covering about one-third of Earth's surface.

questions.question: Loktak Lake, known for its floating 'phumdis', is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Loktak Lake in Manipur has floating phumdis; Keibul Lamjao, the only floating national park, is on it.

questions.question: Which river is popularly called the 'Dakshin Ganga'?
questions.explanation: The Godavari, the longest river of peninsular India, is called Dakshin Ganga (Ganga of the South).

questions.question: The headquarters of the Reserve Bank of India is located in:
questions.explanation: RBI was set up in 1935 at Calcutta; its central office moved permanently to Mumbai in 1937.

questions.question: Which gas do green plants absorb from the atmosphere during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants use CO₂ and water in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll to make glucose, releasing oxygen.

questions.question: Deficiency of vitamin C causes:
questions.explanation: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy (bleeding gums). Rickets – vitamin D; beriberi – vitamin B1; night blindness – vitamin A.

questions.question: Which blood components help in the clotting of blood?
questions.explanation: Platelets (thrombocytes) release clotting factors at a wound to start blood coagulation.

questions.question: Which metal is present at the centre of the chlorophyll molecule?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll has a magnesium ion at the centre of its porphyrin ring; haemoglobin has iron.

questions.question: The term 'bully' is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: 'Bully' is the old method of starting/restarting play in hockey.

questions.question: Garba is a famous folk dance of which state?
questions.explanation: Garba is performed in Gujarat, especially during Navratri.

questions.question: National Sports Day in India is celebrated on 29 August to mark the birth anniversary of:
questions.explanation: 29 August is the birth anniversary of hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand (born 1905).

questions.question: The United Nations Organisation was established in which year?
questions.explanation: The UN came into existence on 24 October 1945, observed as UN Day.

questions.question: The Railway Protection Force (RPF) functions under which ministry?
questions.explanation: RPF is an armed force of the Union under the Railway Protection Force Act, 1957, administered by the Ministry of Railways.

questions.question: Which of the following is an input device of a computer?
questions.explanation: A keyboard feeds data into the computer; monitor, printer and speaker are output devices.

questions.question: What is the smallest number that must be subtracted from 1000 so that the result is exactly divisible by 27?
questions.explanation: 27 × 37 = 999, so 1000 leaves remainder 1. Subtract 1.

questions.question: What is the sum of all prime numbers between 10 and 30?
The product of two numbers is 1,620 and their HCF is 9. What is their LCM?
questions.explanation: LCM = product ÷ HCF = 1620 ÷ 9 = 180.

questions.question: If A's salary is 25% more than B's salary, by what percentage is B's salary less than A's?
40% of a number is 72. What is the number?
Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 5. If 9 is added to each, the ratio becomes 3 : 4. What is the larger number?
The average of five consecutive odd numbers is 27. What is the largest of them?
questions.explanation: The middle number equals the average, 27. The numbers are 23, 25, 27, 29, 31.

questions.question: The average weight of 30 students is 40 kg. When the teacher's weight is included, the average increases by 0.5 kg. What is the teacher's weight?
questions.explanation: New total = 31 × 40.5 = 1255.5 kg; old total = 1200 kg. Teacher = 55.5 kg.

questions.question: An article bought for ₹400 is sold for ₹460. What is the profit percentage?
Two successive discounts of 20% and 10% are equivalent to a single discount of:
In how many years will a sum of money double itself at 12.5% per annum simple interest?
questions.explanation: To double, SI = P: P = P × 12.5 × T/100 ⇒ T = 100/12.5 = 8 years.

questions.question: What is the compound interest on ₹10,000 for 1 year at 20% per annum, compounded half-yearly?
questions.explanation: Half-yearly rate = 10%, 2 periods. Amount = 10000 × 1.1² = ₹12,100. CI = ₹2,100.

questions.question: A can finish a work in 10 days and B in 15 days. In how many days can they finish it working together?
questions.explanation: 1/10 + 1/15 = 5/30 = 1/6, so together they take 6 days.

questions.question: A person covers 36 km in 45 minutes. What is his speed in km/h?
A rectangular field is 40 m long and 25 m wide. What is the cost of fencing it all around at ₹15 per metre?
In a right-angled triangle the two sides containing the right angle are 9 cm and 12 cm. What is the length of the perpendicular drawn from the right-angle vertex to the hypotenuse?
Bird : Nest :: Bee : ?
questions.explanation: A bird lives in a nest; a bee lives in a hive.

questions.question: Select the number that completes the analogy. 6 : 42 :: 8 : ?
Select the odd one out: Wheat, Rice, Maize, Mango
questions.explanation: Wheat, rice and maize are cereal crops; mango is a fruit.

questions.question: Select the odd pair: 3 – 27, 4 – 64, 5 – 125, 6 – 206
questions.explanation: In each pair the second number is the cube of the first: 3³ = 27, 4³ = 64, 5³ = 125. But 6³ = 216, not 206.

questions.question: Find the next number: 7, 14, 28, 56, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is doubled: 56 × 2 = 112.

questions.question: Find the next number: 2, 3, 5, 9, 17, ?
questions.explanation: Differences are 1, 2, 4, 8, so the next difference is 16: 17 + 16 = 33.

questions.question: Find the next term: ACE, FHJ, KMO, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 5 places forward: A→F→K→P, C→H→M→R, E→J→O→T.

questions.question: In a certain code, TEACHER is written as VGCEJGT. How is STUDENT written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter is moved two places forward: S→U, T→V, U→W, D→F, E→G, N→P, T→V.

questions.question: In a certain code, MOTHER is written as NLGSVI. How is FATHER written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite letter (A↔Z, B↔Y, …; position p → 27 − p): M→N, O→L, T→G, H→S, E→V, R→I. So F→U, A→Z, T→G, H→S, E→V, R→I = UZGSVI.

questions.question: If P means '÷', Q means '×', R means '+' and S means '−', what is the value of 36 P 4 Q 3 R 8 S 5?
A is B's sister. C is B's mother. D is C's father. How is A related to D?
questions.explanation: A is a daughter of C (being B's sister). D is C's father, so A is D's granddaughter.

questions.question: A man walks 4 km east and then 3 km north. What is the shortest distance between his starting point and his present position?
questions.explanation: Shortest distance = √(4² + 3²) = √25 = 5 km.

questions.question:
Statements: All pencils are erasers. Some erasers are sharpeners.
Conclusions: I. Some pencils are sharpeners. II. Some sharpeners are erasers.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: 'Some erasers are sharpeners' converts to 'Some sharpeners are erasers' (II). The sharpeners may lie in the part of erasers outside pencils, so I is not certain.

questions.question: A, B, C, D and E sit in a row facing north. D sits at the left end. E sits to the immediate right of D. B sits second from the right end. C does not sit at the right end. Who sits in the middle?
questions.explanation: D = 1, E = 2, B = 4. C and A take 3 and 5; C is not at the right end, so C = 3 (middle) and A = 5.

questions.question: In a group of 100 people, 65 speak Hindi and 45 speak English. Every person speaks at least one of the two languages. How many speak both?
Meena ranks 9th from the top and 26th from the bottom in her class. How many students are there in the class?
Find the missing number: (2, 3, 13), (4, 5, 41), (6, 7, ?)
questions.explanation: Third number = sum of squares of the first two: 4 + 9 = 13, 16 + 25 = 41, so 36 + 49 = 85.

questions.question:
Statement: Regular exercise keeps the body fit. Ramesh exercises regularly.
Conclusions: I. Ramesh is likely to be fit. II. Ramesh does not eat junk food.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: I follows from the two given facts. Nothing is said about Ramesh's diet, so II does not follow.
